messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Discharge Summary

Patient Name: [redacted]
Medical Record Number: [redacted]
Admission Date: [redacted]
Discharge Date: [redacted]
Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Principal Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:

The patient presented with severe right hypochondrium pain along with weight loss and alteration of general condition lasting for six months. The physical examination and laboratory examination were unremarkable. However, abdominal ultrasonography showed a 2.6 cm diameter intraluminal polypoid hyperechoic mass in the gallbladder. Computed tomography scan confirmed the presence of a gallbladder tumor that appeared as an enhancing pedunculated tumor without thickening of the gallbladder wall. A TDM scan showed a cortical fleshy nodule of the right kidney. 

The patient underwent an open cholecystectomy with a partial liver resection. The cholecystectomy specimen showed a metastatic renal cell carcinoma without any involvement of the gallbladder wall. A right radical nephrectomy was carried out through a right subcostal incision, and the histological study revealed a typical conventional clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

The patient was transferred to the department of Urology for further treatment. Following the nephrectomy, the patient recovered well with appropriate management of the surgical wounds.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Medications:

None

Follow-up Plan:

The patient was advised to follow up with the department of Urology as per recommended schedule for a further course of treatment.	

Disposition:

The patient was discharged in stable condition.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
The principal diagnosis here is a metastasis to the gallbladder from a renal cell carcinoma. The gallbladder was the presenting problem and was the focus of the first operation. The primary tumour was in the kidney, which was found afterwards and treated with nephrectomy.

Following the pattern of Example 6 (secondary deposits coded to C79), the options are:
- C79 for the secondary site: the gallbladder is a secondary malignant neoplasm of another specified site, coded C79.8.
- C64 for the primary renal cell carcinoma, which was also treated with nephrectomy.

The admission was for the gallbladder mass, which led to cholecystectomy with partial liver resection. The patient was then transferred to Urology for the nephrectomy. The primary tumour was treated in the same episode, so C64 is a reasonable choice. The usual rule for a known primary with metastases is to code the condition that was the main reason for treatment. Here the primary was unknown at presentation, and the workup and first surgery were directed at the gallbladder metastasis. The nephrectomy was then done in the same admission.

Overall, the primary kidney cancer was the condition ultimately treated and is the underlying cause of everything else. I'll go with C64.

**C64**
